kpis.name: Coder Utilization Rate
kpis.question: Do we have enough coders, and are they busy?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of coders with at least one active allocation (va_allocations where va_allocation_status = 'active') Denominator: COUNT of coders who can code at least one case in the DM's subtree (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul): project grants, grants on in-scope (project, site) pairs, and unit grants that are ancestors or descendants of the DM's unit, excluding ancestors above coding_scope_level_id when the project is view_only. For a project or site DM this equals all active coders of its scope. See [Access Control Model](access-control-model.md). Rate: N / D × 100 Time Frame: Snapshot Actionable: If utilization is low (<70%), coders are idle — either not enough forms in their language or forms aren't being allocated. If high (>95%), coders are saturated — need more coders.
definition.base: coders who can code a case in the DM's subtree (coder availability)

kpis.name: Language Gap Alert
kpis.question: Which ready cases have no coder for their language?

definition.measure: Definition: COUNT of submissions in the ready pool (ready_for_coding) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) where va_narration_language has zero available coders. A coder matches when lower(trim(language)) equals lower(trim(va_narration_language)); a coder with no languages matches any language. Coders are counted for the DM's subtree (coder availability). Source: va_submissions JOIN va_users.vacode_language via grants Scope: ready pool Time Frame: Snapshot Drill-down: Which languages, how many submissions affected
definition.base: ready pool; coders by coder availability

kpis.name: % Uncoded (Pending Rate)
kpis.question: How much is uncoded, and when will it clear?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT in the 6 pending states (screening_pending, attachment_sync_pending, smartva_pending, ready_for_coding, coding_in_progress, coder_step1_saved) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Denominator: COUNT of CODING-POOL Rate: N / D × 100 Scope: CODING-POOL Time Frames: Snapshot, also daily in grid Meaning: What fraction of the eligible pipeline has NOT been coded yet

thresholds.text: Lower is better. Days to clear above 30 means more coders or faster coding are needed.

kpis.name: Daily Inflow vs Outflow
kpis.question: Are we keeping up (inflow against outflow)?

definition.measure: Inflow: COUNT of events that day whose previous_state is outside the pending set and current_state is inside it (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul), so a case entering through SmartVA failure, a reset or an admin override counts too Outflow: COUNT of non-demo events that day whose previous_state is pending and current_state is not (cases leaving the pending set, which includes finalizing); demo events excluded Net delta: Inflow − Outflow Display: Side-by-side bar chart (inflow vs outflow per day, last 7d) Actionable: If inflow consistently exceeds outflow, backlog will grow. Positive net delta = falling behind. Negative = catching up.

thresholds.text: Net inflow minus outflow above 0 means falling behind; below 0 means catching up.

kpis.name: Blocked Forms Alert (Composite)
kpis.question: What is stopping cases, why, how old, and who can unblock them?

definition.measure: Definition: COUNT and breakdown of all submissions that cannot be routed to a coder right now, grouped by blockage reason (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul). Every row except the two upstream rows is restricted to the 6 pending states, so a coded case with a flagged ODK review state or a missing language is not blocked. The upstream rows are coded cases waiting on a DM and stay in the total. One FILTER query. Breakdown: Overlap handling: A single submission may have multiple conditions (e.g., not-codeable AND ODK-has-issues). The breakdown counts each condition independently (a form can appear in multiple rows). A separate "total blocked" count deduplicates by counting each form once, assigned to its primary blockage (highest-priority condition in the order listed above). Display: Table showing blockage type + count + action. Total blocked count shown separately. Scope: pending states plus the upstream states (excludes consent_refused — that's a hard gate) Note on soft gates: not_codeable_by_data_manager and not_codeable_by_coder forms are excluded from CODING-POOL but tracked separately in C-05/D-QG-01/D-QG-02. They are NOT double-counted here. However, if ODK data updates and makes a not-codeable form potentially codeable, it would re-enter the screening pipeline. Time Frame: Snapshot Actionable: This is the DM's "to-do list" — each blockage type has a clear action. DM works through the list to unblock forms and increase throughput. Owner of each blocker row (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-r5s0): screening, upstream change and the soft gates: the DM; attachment sync and SmartVA: the DM, or admin when the queue is down; language gap and "no coder at unit": the coder supervisor or in-charge; sent back and ODK flagged: the field team, through the IC. Sent back also carries the former "awaiting correction" figure: its age (p50 and max), owner ("interviewer, through the IC") and by=interviewer (web only). Every C-23 row gains an intake_source split.

thresholds.text: Lower is better; 0 expected. Each row names an owner (see below).

kpis.name: Pipeline Aging (Stagnation)
kpis.question: Which states hold cases too long?

definition.measure: Definition: COUNT of submissions where workflow_state = 'ready_for_coding' AND workflow_updated_at < now() − interval '48 hours' Also report: Same count at thresholds: >48h, >7d, >30d Source: va_submission_workflow JOIN va_forms for scope Scope: CODING-POOL (ready pool, ready_for_coding only, by design) Time Frame: Snapshot
definition.base: ready pool for the ready_for_coding count; every non-terminal state for the stagnation table

thresholds.text: Per-state normal, alert and critical thresholds (kept from D-WF-03).

kpis.name: Time to Code (Min / Max / Median / P90)
kpis.question: How long does a coding episode take?

definition.measure: Definition: For each finalize event in the window, compute finalize.event_created_at − latest start.event_created_at, where the latest start is the most recent coding_started or recode_started event at or before the finalize (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul). A recoded case yields one duration per finalize, never one per start/finalize combination. Aggregates: MIN, MAX, PERCENTILE(0.5), PERCENTILE(0.90) Source: va_submission_workflow_events rows of the same va_sid, each coder_finalized/recode_finalized paired by a lateral lookup with its latest start Scope: CODING-POOL Inclusions: First-pass coding AND recode episodes Exclusions: Demo events (shared demo predicate) Time Frames: Today, yesterday, 7d

sources: va_submission_workflow_events rows of the same va_sid, each coder_finalized/recode_finalized paired by a lateral lookup with its latest start

kpis.name: State Velocity
kpis.question: Which stage dominates end-to-end time, and where is the bottleneck against peers?

definition.measure: Definition: Average time submissions spend in each workflow state before transitioning out Source: CTE on va_submission_workflow_events computing per-transition durations, aggregated per previous_state Aggregates: AVG, P50, P90 in hours Response: states[] with state, label, transition_count, avg_hours, p50_hours, p90_hours Rendering: Table with sortable columns, slow states highlighted Endpoint: GET /api/v1/analytics/dm-kpi/workflow/state-velocity?days=30 Time Frame: 30d (configurable up to 90d)

sources: CTE on va_submission_workflow_events computing per-transition durations, aggregated per previous_state

kpis.name: Sync Error Rate
kpis.question: Is ODK sync working?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of va_sync_runs where status IN ('error', 'partial') and started_at ≥ window_start Denominator: COUNT of all va_sync_runs where started_at ≥ window_start Rate: N / D × 100 Time Frames: 7d, cumulative

kpis.name: Daily Operations Grid
kpis.question: What came in and what got coded each day?

definition.measure: A 7-column table, last 8 rows (today + 7 prior days), slicable by project and site.
definition.base: ALL-SYNCED for received; coded events for output

kpis.name: Final Cause Coverage
kpis.question: What share of codeable cases has an authoritative cause?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of CODING-POOL submissions with an authoritative final cause (va_final_cod_authority; the WHO 2026 bucket is read from the COD snapshot MV, authoritative_who_bucket). Denominator: COUNT of CODING-POOL, less not_codeable_by_coder (the codeable cases). Rate: N / D × 100. Shown only when D is 20 or more. Replaces: the area dashboard "Final COD" column, the Site-PI "coded" count, and the "achieved" half of C-18. C-18 is the forecast of this KPI. Time Frames: Snapshot, daily series.

thresholds.text: Higher is better; the forecast is C-18.

kpis.name: Reported-Death Interview Coverage
kpis.question: Are reported deaths being interviewed, and how many have waited over 30 days? (death-register projects only)

definition.measure: Applies to death-register projects only (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-r5s0). A project without a death register has no reported-death base, and the KPI is not computed for it. Reported deaths: register rows of the project, with confirmed duplicates excluded. Numerator: reported deaths that have an interview (a linked submission). Denominator: reported deaths. Rate: N / D × 100. Shown only when D is 20 or more. Waiting over 30 days: COUNT of reported deaths with no interview whose report is more than 30 days old. It is a count, owned by the field team through the in-charge, and is the blocker view of this KPI. Time Frames: Snapshot, daily series. Gap: death to interview time exists only for register cases.

thresholds.text: Higher is better; the count waiting over 30 days should fall.

kpis.name: % Not Codeable (Overall)
kpis.question: How many cases are lost to coding, by whom and why?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT where workflow_state IN ('not_codeable_by_coder', 'not_codeable_by_data_manager') Denominator: COUNT of ALL-SYNCED Rate: N / D × 100 Scope: ALL-SYNCED Time Frames: Today, 7d, cumulative Drill-down: By actor (coder vs DM) and by reason
definition.base: ALL-SYNCED (rate); CODING-POOL for the coder share

kpis.name: Not Analysable Rate
kpis.question: How many interviews cannot be analysed, and why?

definition.measure: Was "Consent Refusal Rate"; renamed 2026-10-01 (digitva-4tb). One bucket for every interview that cannot be analysed, whatever the reason. Numerator: COUNT where workflow_state = 'consent_refused'. That state holds every web interview stored as refused, respondent_unavailable or partially_completed, and ODK submissions with consent = no. Per-reason subtext: Refused / Respondent unavailable / Partially completed, read from the active payload's interview_outcome; a payload without one (every ODK submission) counts as Refused. Derived at query time, nothing stored: the API serves it as not_analysable.by_reason, the dashboard card as not_analysable_by_reason. The old consent_refused response key is kept with the same count. The daily grid shows the total only (owner, 2026-10-10: keep the grid simple). The per-reason split lives on the C-06 card and the dashboard card, not in the grid; stored grid days hold no reasons, and splitting them would mean estimates. Denominator: COUNT of ALL-SYNCED Rate: N / D × 100 Time Frames: Today, 7d, cumulative Outcome (what the results say: cause quality, equity and cause mix.) Categories: coding quality, equity.

kpis.name: Unknown Cause Share
kpis.question: What share of finals has no meaningful cause?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of authoritative finals whose WHO 2026 VA cause section is "Cause of death unknown" (UNKNOWN_CAUSE_SECTION). The measure is based on VA causes, per the owner's decision of 2026-10-27. Senility (R54) and other ill-defined codes all map there. An ICD breakdown inside the section is an optional drill-down. Denominator: COUNT of authoritative finals. Rate: N / D × 100. Shown only when D is 20 or more. Meaning: a final that exists but tells the programme nothing. High values point at coding quality, not at volume. Time Frames: Snapshot, weekly series.

kpis.name: Coder-Reviewer Disagreement Rate
kpis.question: Do coders and reviewers agree, at the WHO 2026 bucket level?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of submissions with an active coder final and an active reviewer final whose WHO 2026 bucket differs (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul). Compared from the COD snapshot MV (va_submission_cod_snapshot_mv: coder_final_who_bucket vs reviewer_final_who_bucket), not va_conclusive_cod text; where no bucket exists, the ICD-11 primary stem or ICD-10 code is compared instead. ICD-10 A/B post-coordinated codes compare by primary stem. Denominator: COUNT of submissions with both coder final assessment AND reviewer final assessment (active) Rate: N/D × 100 Source: va_submission_cod_snapshot_mv (refreshed hourly, so the rate can lag a recent finalization) Time Frame: Cumulative
definition.base: submissions with both an active coder final and an active reviewer final

sources: va_submission_cod_snapshot_mv (refreshed hourly, so the rate can lag a recent finalization)

kpis.name: Female Share Against Peers
kpis.question: Are female deaths under-reported in some districts, against peers?

definition.measure: Measure: the female share of cases with sex known, per district (or per block in a district view), against the median of its siblings inside the viewer's grant. Gap: unit female share minus peer median, in percentage points. A district that is well below its peers may be under-reporting female deaths. Base: ALL-SYNCED with sex known. Sex values are raw strings today; they are normalised to female, male and unknown in one place. Suppression: a unit with fewer than 20 cases shows its count with no share, gap or rank. Not claimed: this is composition against peers, not a per-population rate. There is no population figure; expected female share (DHS or SRS, digitva-1835) and SES, caste and education (digitva-r9lk) are later. Time Frames: Cumulative, monthly series.

thresholds.text: Gap to the peer median; a large negative female gap is the signal.

kpis.name: Female-Male Final Cause Gap
kpis.question: Do female cases get a final cause as often as male cases?

definition.measure: Measure: the share of female CODING-POOL cases with an authoritative final cause, minus the same share for male cases. Gap: female rate minus male rate, in percentage points. Sex is normalised as in EQ-01; unknown sex is left out and reported by EQ-03. Register half (death-register projects only): the share of reported female deaths that have an interview, minus the male share. It applies to death-register projects only (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-r5s0); other projects show the final-cause half alone. Suppression: each sex needs a denominator of 20 or more; otherwise counts only. Time Frames: Cumulative, monthly series.

kpis.name: Coder Roster
kpis.question: Who are the active coders, with languages and load?

definition.measure: Definition: Per project, for each active coder: name, email, vacode_language list, total forms coded (cumulative), currently allocated count, active since date Source: va_users JOIN va_user_access_grants JOIN va_final_assessments COUNT Time Frame: Cumulative Note: Policy-only definition, not a dashboard widget

sources: va_users JOIN va_user_access_grants JOIN va_final_assessments COUNT

kpis.name: Staff per Unit
kpis.question: How many staff hold each role in each unit?

definition.measure: Measure: COUNT of active grant holders by role in each unit of the viewer's subtree (coders, reviewers, data managers, interviewers, supervisors). Output: counts only. Names stay in D-LC-06 (web only). Why: the input half of capacity: C-21 says whether coders are busy; ST-01 says how many people there are to do the work. Time Frames: Snapshot. Process (how cases move: flow, timeliness, coding quality, system health and the correction loop.) Categories: flow, timeliness, coding quality, system, loop.
definition.base: active grants in the viewer's subtree

kpis.name: Mean Daily Coding Rate
kpis.question: How many cases does the team code per day?

definition.measure: Definition: Average number of submissions coded per day over the trailing window Formula: COUNT of non-demo finalize events over the window (live, viewer-timezone days) / COUNT of days in window (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Also report: Per coder: SUM of coder_finalized events / days grouped by va_finassess_by Per language: SUM of coder_finalized events / days grouped by va_submissions.va_narration_language Scope: CODING-POOL Time Frames: 7d Actionable: Tells the DM "your team is averaging N forms/day" — compare against inflow rate to know if you're keeping up

kpis.name: Language with Maximum Pendency
kpis.question: Which languages have the most pending cases?

definition.measure: Definition: For each language, COUNT in the 6 pending states (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul), ordered DESC Display: Table: Language | Pending | Coders Available | Gap (yes/no) | Predicted Days to Clear Top row = the bottleneck language Scope: CODING-POOL (6 pending states) Time Frame: Snapshot Actionable: Immediately tells DM which language needs urgent coder recruitment or reallocation

kpis.name: CONSORT Pipeline Flowchart
kpis.question: How many cases are in each workflow state?

definition.measure: Definition: Current count of submissions in each of the 14 workflow states, rendered as a CONSORT-style flowchart with: Main trunk flowing top-to-bottom through pipeline stages Branch points showing terminal states (consent_refused, not_codeable_by_*, finalized_upstream_changed) Flow-through numbers at each stage (total minus cumulative branches) Sub-phases within states (e.g., coder_finalized split by within/beyond the project's recode window) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Optional states visually distinguished from mandatory trunk states Source: va_submission_workflow GROUP BY workflow_state, scoped by DM sites Response includes: total_synced: total submissions in DM scope nodes[]: each node with id, label, count (in state), flow_through (reached this stage), type (trunk/optional/terminal/branch), phase, branch_from sub_phases for coder_finalized: within_window and beyond_window counts, with within_24h and beyond_24h kept for one release (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) conversion: consent_valid_rate, coding_completion_rate, review_rate Rendering: CSS-based flowchart (no chart library). Vertical trunk with horizontal branches. Color-coded by phase. Endpoint: GET /api/v1/analytics/dm-kpi/workflow/flowchart Time Frame: Snapshot

sources: va_submission_workflow GROUP BY workflow_state, scoped by DM sites

kpis.name: Daily State Transitions
kpis.question: How many cases entered each state each day?

definition.measure: Definition: How many submissions entered each state per day over the trailing window Extends C-19 (which tracks crossings of the pending boundary) to ALL states Source: va_submission_workflow_events GROUP BY DATE(event_created_at), current_state Response: days[] with date, transitions (dict of state→count), total Rendering: Stacked bar chart (Chart.js), one bar per day, stacked by target state, color-coded by phase Endpoint: GET /api/v1/analytics/dm-kpi/workflow/daily-transitions?days=7 Time Frame: 7d (configurable up to 90d)

kpis.name: Upstream Change Resolution Time
kpis.question: How long do ODK upstream changes take to resolve?

definition.measure: Numerator: For each resolved upstream change in 7d, resolved_at − created_at Aggregate: PERCENTILE(0.5) Source: va_submission_upstream_changes Note: rows exist for ODK changes only, so send-backs and reopens are already excluded Time Frame: 7d

kpis.name: % Forms Reviewed
kpis.question: What share of coded cases has been reviewed?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of submissions that have at least one va_reviewer_final_assessments row with active status Denominator: COUNT of submissions that ever reached coder_finalized (i.e., CODED scope, excluding those still in coder-finalized if reviewer window hasn't passed) Refined denominator: COUNT where workflow_state IN ('reviewer_eligible', 'reviewer_coding_in_progress', 'reviewer_finalized') OR has a reviewer_finalized event in history Rate: N / D × 100 Scope: CODED Time Frames: 7d, cumulative Note: The project's recode window (recode_window_minutes, not a fixed 24 h) means reviewer-eligible forms can't be reviewed immediately. Denominator excludes coder_finalized forms younger than that window (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul).

kpis.name: Reopen Rate
kpis.question: How often are finalized cases reopened for recoding?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of events with transition_id IN ('upstream_change_accepted', 'admin_override_to_recode') in window, minus events whose transition_reason is interviewer_revision (the interviewer's revision restarting a sent-back case) or interview_chosen (a supervisor's choice of the other interview); neither is a data-manager reopen Companion: d_wt_04_revision_restarts_7d counts the interviewer_revision restarts Denominator: COUNT of coder_finalized events in window Rate: N/D × 100 Scope: CODED Meaning: What fraction of finalized forms were re-opened for recoding Time Frames: 7d, cumulative

kpis.name: Share of Fast Finals
kpis.question: What share of finals was finished suspiciously fast?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of non-demo finalize events whose time to code (see canonical terms) is under the registry cut-off. Denominator: COUNT of non-demo finalize events in the window. Rate: N / D × 100. Shown only when D is 20 or more. By coder: per-coder rows name people, so they are web only, for DMs in scope; MCP returns totals. Cut-off: 180 seconds by default. This is elapsed time between workflow events, not time on screen. Time Frames: 7d, cumulative.

kpis.name: Sync Latency (ODK → App)
kpis.question: How long does a submission take to reach DigitVA from ODK?

definition.measure: Definition: For submissions synced in window: time between ODK submission timestamp and local DB insert Formula: va_created_at − va_submission_date per submission, ODK-sourced forms only (form_source = 'odk') (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Aggregates: P50, P90, P99 Time Frames: Today, 7d

kpis.name: Attachment Health
kpis.question: How many ODK submissions are missing their attachments?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of ODK-sourced submissions past SmartVA gate where attachment count = 0 (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Denominator: COUNT of ODK-sourced submissions past SmartVA gate Rate: N / D × 100 Source: va_submission_attachments JOIN va_submissions Time Frame: Snapshot
definition.base: ODK-sourced submissions past the SmartVA gate

kpis.name: Attachment Download Completeness
kpis.question: Did the last sync download its attachments?

definition.measure: Numerator: va_sync_runs.attachment_downloaded from latest run Denominator: the same run's attachment_forms_total (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) (the code's denominator; the earlier text said downloaded + skipped + errors) Rate: N/D × 100 Time Frame: Snapshot

kpis.name: SmartVA Failure Rate
kpis.question: How often does SmartVA fail?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of va_smartva_runs where va_smartva_outcome = 'failed' in window Denominator: COUNT of all va_smartva_runs in window Rate: N/D × 100 Time Frames: 7d, cumulative

kpis.name: ODK Coverage Delta
kpis.question: Does ODK Central hold more submissions than DigitVA?

definition.measure: Definition: Per form, ODK-side submission count (from preview) minus local COUNT Source: Sync preview logic (live ODK call) Time Frame: On-demand

kpis.name: Send-back and Reopen Rate by Reason
kpis.question: How often are cases sent back or reopened, and why?

definition.measure: Collect only. Send-back and reopen exist only for Collect-sourced cases; ODK submissions are refused, and ODK uses hasIssues plus Central edits instead. The split is va_forms.form_source. Browser against device is not split. Numerator: COUNT of send-back and reopen workflow events (sent_back_for_revision, reopened_for_revision) in the window. Denominator: COUNT of finalize events in the window. Reason: read from the submission audit row (<reason>:<code>), paired with the workflow event by LATERAL. by=actor_role is available. ODK proxy: hasIssues plus upstream-change counts, shown as a proxy only. ODK review-state history is not stored, so ODK reasons, time to correct and repeat flags are not captured. Per-interviewer rows name people: web only, for DMs and ICs in scope, and never sent over MCP. Time Frames: 7d, cumulative.

kpis.name: Time to Correct
kpis.question: How long does a correction take, send-back to revision?

definition.measure: Collect only. See CL-01. Measure: each correction request paired with the next interviewer_revision event. Median and p90 of the gap, in hours. Open and cancelled requests: counted, with no duration. Critical path: it is the "correction" stage of the D-WF-02 critical path. ODK: not captured, because ODK review-state history is not stored. Time Frames: 7d, cumulative.

kpis.name: Supervisor Review Turnaround
kpis.question: How long does supervisor review take?

definition.measure: Inactive until digitva-ydnl.4 ships. Measure: time from a case being submitted for supervisor review to the supervisor's decision. Median and p90 in hours. Scope: only projects that have the supervisor review switch on. Time Frames: 7d, cumulative. Output (what the process produces: coded cases, coverage, data quality and workforce output.) Categories: flow, coverage, data quality, workforce, loop.
definition.base: projects with the supervisor review switch on

thresholds.text: Lower is better. Inactive until digitva-ydnl.4 ships.

kpis.name: Predicted vs Achieved (Burndown)
kpis.question: Are we ahead of or behind the target-date trajectory?

definition.measure: Definition: Chart comparing projected completion trajectory vs actual cumulative coding progress Projected line: At project start (or target date set), draw a straight line from (start, total_forms) to (target_date, 0). Daily point: total − (days_elapsed × daily_target_rate) Achieved line: Cumulative CODED submissions over time, rebuilt live from workflow events, not from va_daily_kpi_aggregates (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Requires: project_target_completion_date set by admin Display: Line chart, two lines, X-axis = time, Y-axis = remaining forms Actionable: If achieved line is above projected line, the project is behind schedule. The gap tells the DM exactly how far behind. Time Frame: Daily series from project start to target date

thresholds.text: Achieved line above projected line means behind schedule.

periods: Daily series from project start to target date

kpis.name: Social Autopsy Completion Rate
kpis.question: What share of coded cases has a social autopsy?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of submissions with at least one active va_social_autopsy_analyses row (where va_saa_status = 'active') Denominator: COUNT of CODED submissions WHERE the submission's own project has social_autopsy_enabled = true (joined on the form's project) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Rate: N/D × 100 Inclusions: Only projects where social_autopsy_enabled = true Exclusions: Projects where social_autopsy_enabled = false Time Frame: Cumulative

kpis.name: Submission Language Distribution
kpis.question: What languages are the interviews in?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT grouped by lower(trim(va_narration_language)) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) ("English" and "english" are one group) Denominator scope: CONSENT-VALID Where: va_narration_language IS NOT NULL Time Frame: Cumulative Also report: Trend over time (monthly)

kpis.name: Visit Notes
kpis.question: Where are interviews not completed (refused or respondent unavailable), and is each visit documented?

definition.measure: Count: supervised cases whose active payload holds a visit note (visit_date, visit_address, visit_remarks, recorded with a refused or unavailable interview outcome). This is the same predicate as the supervision and submissions visit_note=1 filter, by unit. Privacy: address and remarks are never part of the KPI. Viewers that should_redact_pii sees only the date, and MCP returns counts only. Applies to DigitVA Collect and web intake. ODK has no visit note. Time Frames: Snapshot, weekly.
definition.base: supervised Collect cases in the viewer's scope

kpis.name: ODK Has Issues Count
kpis.question: How many cases does ODK flag with issues?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT where va_odk_reviewstate = 'hasIssues' Denominator: ALL-SYNCED Time Frame: Cumulative

kpis.name: Forms with Missing/Unmapped Language
kpis.question: How many cases have no usable language?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT where va_narration_language IS NULL OR va_narration_language = '' OR va_narration_language NOT IN (SELECT alias FROM map_language_aliases) Denominator: COUNT of CODING-POOL Rate: N/D × 100 Scope: CODING-POOL Time Frame: Snapshot Actionable: These forms cannot be language-matched to coders. Either the ODK form doesn't collect language, the value isn't in the alias mapping table, or the field is blank. DM action: check alias mapping, update ODK form, or manually assign language

kpis.name: % Forms with Upstream Changes
kpis.question: How many coded cases had ODK data change after finalization?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of submissions that have at least one va_submission_workflow_events row with transition_id = 'upstream_change_detected' whose transition_reason is not a revision request (sent_back_for_revision, reopened_for_revision) or interview_chosen: ODK changes only Denominator: COUNT of CODED submissions Rate: N / D × 100 Scope: CODED Time Frames: 7d, cumulative Meaning: What fraction of coded forms had ODK data change after finalization

kpis.name: Locally Missing in ODK
kpis.question: How many local cases no longer exist in ODK?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT where va_sync_issue_code = 'missing_in_odk' (the core analytics MV's odk_missing column) Denominator: ALL-SYNCED *plus* the retired rows themselves — this KPI is the one place that counts them, and it ignores the default exclusion Surfaced as the "Missing in ODK" card on the data-manager dashboard (missing_in_odk_submissions); clicking it filters the list to odk_sync=missing_in_odk Time Frame: Cumulative

kpis.name: NQA Completion Rate
kpis.question: What share of coded cases has a narrative quality assessment?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of submissions with at least one active va_narrative_assessments row (where va_nqa_status = 'active') Denominator: COUNT of CODED submissions WHERE the submission's own project has narrative_qa_enabled = true (joined on the form's project, never a project at the same site) (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul) Rate: N/D × 100 Inclusions: Only projects where narrative_qa_enabled = true Exclusions: Projects where narrative_qa_enabled = false (excluded from both N and D) Time Frame: Cumulative

kpis.name: Language-Not-Codeable Correlation
kpis.question: Do language not-codeable decisions match the coder gap?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of va_coder_review where va_creview_reason = 'narration_language' AND submission's va_narration_language is in the gap set (D-LC-03) Denominator: COUNT of all va_coder_review where va_creview_reason = 'narration_language' Rate: N/D × 100 Time Frame: Cumulative

kpis.name: Sex or Age Unknown
kpis.question: How many cases have sex or age unknown?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of ALL-SYNCED submissions where sex or age is missing or unrecognised. Denominator: COUNT of ALL-SYNCED. Rate: N / D × 100. Meaning: guards the validity of EQ-01 and EQ-02; if it is high, their gaps are not trustworthy. Time Frames: Snapshot, weekly series.

thresholds.text: Lower is better; it guards the validity of EQ-01 and EQ-02.

kpis.name: Coder Throughput
kpis.question: How many cases does each coder finish?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of workflow events with transition_id IN ('coder_finalized', 'recode_finalized') in window Denominator: — (raw count) Also report: Per-coder breakdown Scope: CODING-POOL Time Frames: Today, yesterday, 7d, cumulative Inclusions: Non-demo events only (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-0hul)

kpis.name: Forms per Coder by Language
kpis.question: Which coder codes which language?

definition.measure: Definition: For each coder × language combination, the count of forms coded (cumulative and in last 7d) Display: Heatmap table Numerator: COUNT of va_final_assessments (active) GROUP BY (va_finassess_by, va_submissions.va_narration_language) Denominator scope: CODED Also show: Backlog per language = pending in that language − forms currently being coded in that language Time Frames: 7d, cumulative Actionable: Shows which coders are productive in which languages. DM can reallocate coders to languages with higher backlog. Also shows if a coder claims to know a language but hasn't coded any forms in it.

kpis.name: Reviewer Throughput
kpis.question: How many cases do reviewers finish?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of events with transition_id = 'reviewer_finalized' in window Time Frames: Today, 7d, cumulative

kpis.name: Repeat Send-backs
kpis.question: How many cases were sent back twice or more?

definition.measure: Collect only. See CL-01. Numerator: COUNT of cases with 2 or more correction requests. Denominator: COUNT of cases with at least 1 correction request. Meaning: a case that comes back twice points at an unclear instruction or a field-team gap. Per-interviewer rows name people: web only, never over MCP. Time Frames: Cumulative. Outcome (what the results say: cause quality, equity and cause mix.) Categories: coding quality, cause mix.

kpis.name: Agreement with SmartVA
kpis.question: How often does the final cause agree with SmartVA?

definition.measure: Numerator: COUNT of authoritative finals whose WHO 2026 bucket equals the bucket of the case's SmartVA result. Denominator: COUNT of authoritative finals that have a SmartVA result mapped to a bucket. Rate: N / D × 100. Shown only when D is 20 or more. Meaning: how often the human final and the automated result agree. It is a quality signal, not a target to maximise: SmartVA is an input to coding, not the truth. Time Frames: Cumulative, weekly series.
definition.base: authoritative finals with a SmartVA result

kpis.name: Cause Mix
kpis.question: What is the cause mix?

definition.measure: Measure: COUNT of authoritative finals by WHO 2026 bucket, with the share of each (the cause mix). Base: authoritative finals. Counts under 5 are folded; shares are shown only when the base is 20 or more. Meaning: what the programme is finding. It is context for the quality KPIs, not a performance measure. Answerable from the AI cube (kpi_MO-01 catalog entry). Time Frames: Cumulative, monthly series. Correction-loop facts (owner decision 2026-10-27, digitva-r5s0): Send-back and reopen are Collect only. ODK submissions are refused, and ODK uses hasIssues plus Central edits instead. ODK review-state history is not stored, so ODK time to correct, repeat flags and reasons are not captured. Per-interviewer rows name people, so they are web only, for DMs and ICs in scope, and never sent over MCP. The Collect/ODK split is va_forms.form_source. Browser against device is not split. See also [Interview Revisions Policy](interview-revisions.md).
